newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-SANDOWN PUTS ON TIGHTER SECURITY FOR WHITBREAD.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-SANDOWN PUTS ON TIGHTER SECURITY FOR WHITBREAD.

text.p: Sandown racecourse, acting on police fears of a possible IRA bomb alert, banned all cars from the track and subjected racegoers to a stringent security checks on Saturday.

Racing authorities are taking no chances after the Grand National, the world's most famoust steeplechase was hit earlier this month by a bomb alert. The course was hurredly cleared and the race postponed for 48 hours.
But thousands of racegoers made light of the security at Sandown and joined the 96-year-old Queen Mother for the Whitbread Gold Cup, the last big race of the steeplechasing season.
They all had to park their cars in a nearby school playground and each racegoer was individually searched.

The Irish Republican Army, battling to oust Britain from Northern Ireland, have staged a string of bomb alerts and attacks on motorways, railways and airports in a bid to force Northern Ireland on to the political agenda in the run up to the May 1 British election.
